Where is Sioux Falls and how big has it become?

Sioux Falls is the largest city in South Dakota and the county seat of Minnehaha County, with part of the city reaching into Lincoln County to the south. It sits in the far eastern corner of the state, about 15 miles west of the Minnesota line, where Interstate 29 and Interstate 90 meet.

The city was chartered in 1856 beside the Big Sioux River and takes its name from the falls there. The population was 2,164 in 1880, 81,182 in 1980 and 192,517 in the 2020 census, a gain of 25.1 percent from 2010 to 2020. That pace of growth matters to anyone selling a house here, because it means a steady stream of new subdivisions competes with older neighborhoods for the same buyers.

  • County seat of Minnehaha County, with a northern edge of the city in Lincoln County
  • Government: strong mayor and an eight-member council (five district seats, three at-large)
  • Elevation about 1,463 feet, on the eastern edge of the Great Plains

What do people in Sioux Falls do for work?

Health care, banking and food processing carry the Sioux Falls job market. The 2022 city financial report lists Sanford Health as the largest employer, and the table below shows the next few.

EmployerEmployees (2022 city report)
Sanford Health11,010
Avera Health7,888
Sioux Falls School District3,688
Smithfield Foods (John Morrell)3,400
Hy-Vee2,806
Wells Fargo2,035

Citibank moved its primary credit card center to the city in 1981, and South Dakota has no state corporate income tax, which has helped draw financial companies. For sellers, a job change at one of these employers is a common reason a house goes on the market quickly. Relocation deadlines rarely line up with a traditional listing timeline.

How does Sioux Falls weather affect an older house?

Sioux Falls has a humid continental climate with cold winters and warm summers, and the weather shows up in roofs, basements and heating bills. Foss Field averages 17.9 degrees in January and 74.4 degrees in July, using 1991 to 2020 normals.

  • Snowfall: about 45.3 inches a year
  • Precipitation: about 27.85 inches a year
  • Days at 90 degrees or higher: about 15 a year
  • Days at or below zero: about 25 a year

Freeze and thaw cycles are hard on shingles, gutters, sidewalks and foundation walls. Buyers who finance a purchase often ask for repairs to a worn roof or a damp basement. A cash buyer usually takes those items as they are, which is one reason owners of houses with deferred maintenance look at that route.

What should a Sioux Falls seller know about flood rules?

A house in a mapped floodplain in Sioux Falls carries extra permit rules, and the city enforces them after storm damage. After the flash flooding of June 2024, Planning and Development Services reminded owners that any construction or repair in a floodplain needs a floodplain development permit, even when no building permit is required.

The city also tracks cumulative damage over three years. If repair costs reach 45 percent or more of the structure's pre-flood market value, work cannot start until the owner shows compliance with the floodplain ordinance, which can mean elevating or flood-proofing the building. A seller with a flood-damaged house should ask the city where that line falls before spending money.

On the insurance side, the city reported that it moved to Community Rating System Class 7 on October 1, 2023, which gives 15 percent off National Flood Insurance Program premiums for covered properties. The city said it hoped to reach Class 6, and a 20 percent discount, as early as 2026. Check the city announcement for the current class.

What are the Sioux Falls rules if the house is a rental?

Since January 1, 2024, owners and managers of long-term and short-term residential rentals in Sioux Falls need a city rental permit, even if they registered before. The permit costs $50 per address, and the owner must finish a one-time training course of at least two hours.

  • The permit must be in hand before advertising, soliciting renters or allowing occupancy.
  • One permit is needed for each rental street address.
  • A change of ownership or management must be reported in writing within 30 days.
  • Owners living more than 50 miles from Sioux Falls must name a local contact who can handle upkeep.
  • A permit can be revoked after a fourth violation when three were cited in the previous three calendar years.

Permit transfers carry no fee when written notice is given, so a landlord selling a tenant-occupied house should tell the buyer to file that notice. The city's Code Enforcement team handles nuisance, housing, property maintenance, signs, trees, grass and weeds, and zoning complaints, so an unmowed lot or a pile of debris can turn into a citation before closing.

What paperwork does a South Dakota home sale require?

Three items come up in almost every Sioux Falls sale: a seller's disclosure statement, a certificate of real estate value and the transfer fee. The state real estate commission form, dated 07/2025, says it is required by law to be completed by sellers of real property and given to buyers. It asks about liens, easements, flood plains, the roof, water penetration, radon, lead paint, mold and about 47 systems and appliances.

When a deed is recorded, the register of deeds will not accept it without a Certificate of Real Estate Value (PT 56). It lists the buyer and seller, the legal description, the actual price and the payment terms.

ItemWhat the official source says
Deed recording, Minnehaha County$30.00
Transfer fee, Minnehaha County schedule$1.00 per thousand ($0.50 per $500)
Transfer fee authoritySDCL 43-4-21, with 19 exemptions in SDCL 43-4-22
Certificate of valueRequired for any deed or contract for deed (PT 56)

A house in the part of the city inside Lincoln County is recorded with that county's register of deeds, not Minnehaha's. Confirm the parcel's county on the tax bill before you schedule a closing.

How do property taxes work when a Sioux Falls house sells?

South Dakota taxes are billed a year behind, so the seller usually owes part of the current tax bill at closing. Minnehaha County says taxes are due January 1, with the first half accepted without penalty through April 30 and the second half through October 31. Late payments carry a 10 percent annual penalty.

Owner-occupied status matters for the bill. The classification requires the owner to live in the home on the November 1 assessment date, and after an ownership change the new owner files a new application between November 1 and March 15. Our Sioux Falls property tax guide covers assessments, levies and delinquent taxes in more detail.

Which schools, roads and transit serve a Sioux Falls house?

Most of the city sits in the Sioux Falls School District, which serves more than 23,000 students across 25 elementary, 7 middle and 6 high schools. Augustana University, the University of Sioux Falls and the University of South Dakota Sanford School of Medicine's Sioux Falls campus are also in the city.

Sioux Area Metro runs 16 bus lines within the city, plus paratransit and an on-demand service. Sioux Falls Regional Airport (Joe Foss Field) has commercial flights, and Jefferson Lines runs intercity buses. The nearest Amtrak station is in Omaha, about 200 miles away.

Which way of selling a Sioux Falls house fits your situation?

Listing with an agent usually brings the widest buyer pool, but it comes with showings, inspections, buyer repair requests and commission. Selling it yourself saves commission and adds the paperwork above. A cash offer works best when time, condition or tenants are the problem.

  • Inherited house with an unfinished estate
  • Rental with tenants or an unpaid permit issue
  • Flood or storm damage with repair costs the owner cannot cover
  • Back taxes or a mortgage that is falling behind
  • A relocation with a fixed start date

We buy Sioux Falls houses as-is. Offers depend on the property, and you can turn one down at no cost.

More questions about Sioux Falls, SD

How big is Sioux Falls?

The Census Bureau estimates 213,748 residents as of July 1, 2025, up from 192,517 in the 2020 census. It is the largest city in South Dakota and the seat of Minnehaha County.

Does a Sioux Falls seller have to give a disclosure statement?

Yes. South Dakota's seller's property condition disclosure form says it is required by law for sellers of real property and must go to the buyer. Sellers must amend it in writing if a material fact changes before closing.

What is the transfer fee when a house sells in Minnehaha County?

Minnehaha County's Register of Deeds lists the transfer fee as $1.00 per thousand, or $0.50 per $500, plus a $30.00 recording fee for a deed. SDCL 43-4-22 lists 19 exemptions, such as certain transfers between spouses or parent and child.

Do I need a rental permit to sell a tenant-occupied house in Sioux Falls?

The owner of a rental must hold a city permit at $50 per address. The permit can be transferred without a fee if written notice is given, and ownership changes must be reported within 30 days.

What if my Sioux Falls house is in a floodplain?

Any repair or rebuilding of a flood-damaged structure in a floodplain needs a floodplain development permit. When repair costs reach 45 percent of the pre-flood market value, the owner must show compliance with the floodplain ordinance before work starts.

Which county do I pay taxes to if my house is in Sioux Falls?

It depends on the parcel. Most of the city is in Minnehaha County, and a smaller part is in Lincoln County. Check your tax notice for the county treasurer.

Can I sell a Sioux Falls house with back property tax due?

Yes. Unpaid taxes are settled from the sale proceeds at closing, and the county treasurer can give a payoff figure. Minnehaha County charges a 10 percent annual penalty on late taxes.

Where is Rapid City and how is it laid out?

Rapid City is the county seat of Pennington County and sits on the eastern slope of the Black Hills, at about 3,356 feet. It is the second-largest city in South Dakota, with 74,703 people in the 2020 census and about 156,000 in the metro area.

A low ridge called The Gap splits the city, and it lies on both sides of the Dakota Hogback. The Westside sits in the Red Valley between the Black Hills foothills and the Hogback, while the central and eastern parts of town lie in the Rapid Creek valley. Newer development has pushed into the foothills and north along Interstate 90. A house in the foothills and a house beside the creek face very different risks, so location shapes both value and repair needs.

  • County seat of Pennington County
  • Total area of about 55 square miles
  • Shadow of Black Elk Peak, the highest point east of the Rocky Mountains

What shaped Rapid City's history?

Rapid City began in February 1876 as Hay Camp, founded by a group of unsuccessful miners, and was incorporated in February 1883. It took its name from Rapid Creek and promoted itself as the Gateway to the Black Hills.

The defining event for homeowners came on June 9 and 10, 1972. Nearly 15 inches of rain fell in about six hours near Nemo, Canyon Lake Dam broke that night, and the Black Hills Flood killed 238 people. Property losses topped $160 million, including 1,335 homes. It remains the worst natural disaster in South Dakota history, and it explains why the city takes floodplain permitting seriously today.

Who employs people in Rapid City?

Government, health care and tourism lead the Rapid City economy. Government services in all three tiers, local, state and federal, make up the largest sector.

Sector or employerDetail from the source
Ellsworth Air Force BaseHome of the 28th Bomb Wing and its B-1B bombers, on the city's outskirts
Health careMore than 8,000 jobs, with Monument Health the main system
Federal and state agenciesArmy National Guard (Camp Rapid), National Park Service, US Forest Service, Indian Health Service
TourismTied to Mount Rushmore, Sturgis and Deadwood

A military base means regular transfers in and out. Sellers who receive orders often need to close on a fixed date, and that deadline can be hard to meet with a conventional listing that depends on buyer financing.

How does Rapid City's climate affect a house?

Rapid City is drier than eastern South Dakota and swings between hot summers and long winters. The airport records about 17.44 inches of precipitation a year, 48.5 inches of seasonal snow and about 2,857 hours of sunshine.

  • January mean temperature: 24.3 degrees
  • July mean temperature: 72.4 degrees
  • About 32 days a year at or above 90 degrees
  • Average first freeze: October 4
  • Hardiness zone: 5b

Snow load, quick temperature swings and summer sun wear on roofs, siding and decks. Older homes in the Rapid Creek valley and on the Westside often have original windows and aging heating systems, which a buyer's inspector will flag.

What flood rules apply to a Rapid City property?

Any property inside a Special Flood Hazard Area in Rapid City is subject to FEMA rules and city permits. The city takes part in the National Flood Insurance Program, and FEMA issued its first Flood Insurance Rate Map for the area on February 18, 1998, followed by new maps for Pennington County on June 3, 2013.

The city's floodplain page also lists map revisions, including a Lime Creek remapping effective April 4, 2022, and several drainage-basin revisions since 2017. An owner can check whether a house is in the 100-year floodplain, which means a 1 percent chance of flooding in any year, by contacting the city's Floodplain Administrator at 394-4154.

  • Building or repairing in the floodplain needs a Floodplain Development Permit.
  • Rules are in Rapid City Municipal Code chapters 15.32 and 17.28.
  • An elevation certificate can document a structure's height for insurance.

Details are on the city's Floodplain Management page. A buyer who needs flood insurance will ask, so sellers do well to have the answer ready.

What are Rapid City's vacation rental rules?

Rapid City adopted its first zoning rules for vacation homes on December 2, 2025, by an 8 to 2 council vote under Ordinance No. 6698, with registration opening January 30, 2026. A vacation home is a whole dwelling rented to the public for up to 28 consecutive days and more than 14 days a year, with no owner or manager living there during the rental.

  • Vacation homes with up to five bedrooms are a permitted use in the districts listed.
  • Homes with more than five bedrooms need a conditional use permit.
  • Occupancy is capped at two people per bedroom plus two more.
  • Parking must be provided, and operators need a South Dakota lodging license.

An owner selling a house that was used as a short-term rental should check that registration is current. The buyer may ask for proof of the city registration number and the state license.

How are property taxes handled in Pennington County?

Pennington County bills in arrears: taxes are due January 1, the first half is delinquent after April 30 and the second half after October 31. The Treasurer notes that special assessments are due in full before May 1 and that mortgage companies do not always pay them.

The Equalization Department mails assessment notices on or near March 1. The assessed value reflects market value as of the previous November 1. The county offers a monthly ACH plan in ten payments, with applications due December 15 for the following year.

Two relief programs affect a sale. The Homestead Exemption defers taxes until the property is sold, so deferred taxes with interest must be paid from the proceeds. The Assessment Freeze for seniors and disabled owners requires an application by April 1. The Department of Revenue also lists a municipal property tax reduction for elderly and disabled Rapid City residents. The Treasurer's Office is at 605-394-2163.

What paperwork does a Rapid City sale need?

A South Dakota seller must give the buyer a completed property condition disclosure statement, and the deed needs a Certificate of Real Estate Value (PT 56) to be recorded. The state form, dated 07/2025, asks about liens, easements, flood plains, roof leaks, radon, lead paint, mold and the working status of systems.

The transfer fee is set under SDCL 43-4-21, and SDCL 43-4-22 lists 19 exemptions, including certain transfers between spouses and between parent and child for nominal consideration. As a benchmark, Minnehaha County's schedule shows $1.00 per thousand. Confirm the Pennington County amount with the Register of Deeds.

Which schools, airport and transit serve Rapid City?

Rapid City Area Schools covers the city except the airport territory, which sits in Douglas School District 51-1. The district runs three high schools: Rapid City Central, Stevens and Rapid City High.

Rapid City Regional Airport offers commercial flights to hub cities, and Rapid Ride is the municipal bus service. Jefferson Lines runs intercity buses. There has been no passenger rail since 1960, and freight comes through the Rapid City, Pierre and Eastern Railroad.

When does a cash sale make sense in Rapid City?

A cash sale fits when a deadline, a repair bill or a title problem makes a normal listing hard. Common cases in Rapid City include flood-zone houses, military moves, inherited homes and former vacation rentals.

We buy Rapid City houses as-is. We make no promises on price before we see the property, and you owe nothing if you turn the offer down.

More questions about Rapid City, SD

How many people live in Rapid City?

The Census Bureau estimates 80,589 residents as of July 1, 2025. The 2020 census counted 74,703, making it the second-largest city in South Dakota.

Is my Rapid City house in a floodplain?

You can find out by contacting the city's Floodplain Administrator at 394-4154 or checking the FEMA map. Any building or repair in a Special Flood Hazard Area needs a Floodplain Development Permit.

Can I still sell a house that was a vacation rental in Rapid City?

Yes. Since December 2025, Rapid City has had zoning rules for vacation homes, with registration that opened January 30, 2026. Buyers may ask for the city registration and the South Dakota lodging license.

When are Pennington County property taxes due?

Taxes are due January 1. The first half becomes delinquent after April 30 and the second half after October 31.

What happens to deferred homestead taxes when I sell?

The Homestead Exemption defers taxes until the property is sold, with interest continuing at a reduced rate. The deferred amount comes due at sale.

Does South Dakota require a seller disclosure?

Yes. The state's seller's property condition disclosure statement must be completed and given to the buyer. A written amendment is needed if a material fact changes before closing.

Where is Aberdeen, South Dakota, and how is it laid out?

Aberdeen is in northeastern South Dakota in the James River valley, about 11 miles west of the river. It is the seat of Brown County and, according to the Aberdeen Development Corporation, the third largest city in the state behind Sioux Falls and Rapid City.

The Census Bureau lists the city at 16.652 square miles, and Moccasin Creek, a slow-moving waterway, runs through it. The city was plotted as a town site on January 3, 1881 by a Milwaukee Road railroad official and was officially founded on July 6, 1881, the day the first Milwaukee Road train arrived. The railroad's president, Alexander Mitchell, who was born in Aberdeen, Scotland, chose the name.

The Census Bureau estimated 27,961 residents on July 1, 2025, down 1.8% from the 2020 base of 28,479, after a 2020 census count of 28,495. Those figures are worth keeping in mind when you price a house against a listing.

Measure (Census QuickFacts)Aberdeen
Population, July 1, 2025 estimate27,961
Households, 2020-202412,469
Owner-occupied housing rate, 2020-202461.7%
Median value of owner-occupied homes$217,300
Median monthly owner cost with a mortgage$1,524
Median monthly owner cost without a mortgage$584
Median gross rent$762
Median household income$64,405
Mean commute11.9 minutes

What does the Aberdeen economy look like?

Health care, education and a diverse mix of small employers anchor Aberdeen. The Aberdeen Development Corporation says the city is a hub for health care with two major hospital systems, Avera St. Luke's and Sanford Health, and that the Aberdeen metro area ranks 9th of 542 small cities for industry diversity.

Northern State University sits in the middle of town with more than 3,500 students, and the corporation reports a regional connection to more than 2,600 students at Lake Area Technical College. About 300 bachelor's degree graduates a year enter the workforce, and the development group puts the regional population at 41,971 with a labor force of 22,036 as of August 2023.

The Census Bureau's economic figures show where the money is. In 2022 Aberdeen reported $402.3 million in health care and social assistance receipts and $839.9 million in retail sales. Those totals come from the Economic Census and cover the whole city.

How cold does Aberdeen get, and what does that mean for a house?

Aberdeen has a humid continental climate with hot summers and cold, dry winters. January's average daily temperature is 12.8 degrees Fahrenheit and July's is 72.3 degrees, and the city sees 38 days a year with lows below zero and 16 days of 90 degree highs.

Snowfall totals about 42 inches and precipitation about 21.8 inches a year, mostly in the warmer months. Records run from minus 46 in 1912 to 115 degrees in 1936, and a reading of minus 42 as recently as January 15, 2009.

  • A furnace failure in an empty house is a real risk during a cold snap, so winter vacancies need heat.
  • Roof and gutter condition matter after heavy snow.
  • Cold swings can show up in basement walls and foundations, which a buyer's inspector will ask about.

In April 2023 the city ran a one-week curbside pickup for branches under six inches in diameter that a November ice storm had left behind. If a storm left your yard damaged, a cash buyer does not need it cleaned up first.

How do roads, transit and schools affect an Aberdeen sale?

Two U.S. highways meet the city: US 281 and US 12, which is signed as 6th Avenue South through town, and US 281 was moved onto a bypass around the west side. Aberdeen Regional Airport has Delta Connection flights to Minneapolis-St. Paul, and Jefferson Lines buses connect to Sioux Falls, Fargo and Minneapolis.

Ride Line Transportation Services gives demand-response service, and Aberdeen is described as the largest city in South Dakota without fixed-route transit. The Census Bureau puts the mean commute at 11.9 minutes, so most trips across town are short.

The Aberdeen School District serves the city, with Central High School and Holgate and Simmons middle schools, and parochial options include Roncalli High School. The district lists six elementary schools, so check which one serves a specific address.

Which Brown County offices matter when you sell an Aberdeen house?

Aberdeen houses are taxed and recorded through Brown County. The Treasurer is at 25 Market St., Suite 2, Aberdeen, SD 57401, phone (605) 626-7133, open 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. on weekdays, and no title transfers are started after 4:45 p.m. The Treasurer collects property tax for the county, the city, the school districts and any other taxing district, and also administers tax aid for low-income and elderly families.

The Register of Deeds records deeds, mortgages, satisfactions, easements and similar documents, and its land records go back to the early 1870s. The office does not give legal opinions, so it refers people to an abstractor, a title company or an attorney.

  • The state transfer fee is $0.50 per $500 of value under SDCL 43-4-21, and it applies when there is consideration.
  • Taxes are paid in two halves, and under SDCL 10-21-23 the first half is delinquent on May 1 and the second on November 1 if unpaid.
  • Owner-occupied status is claimed by March 15 with the Director of Equalization, and the home must be owned and occupied on November 1.

The state's formula applies in Aberdeen like everywhere else: assessed at market value, taxed on 85% of it, and billed at the combined levy of the county, the city and the school district.

How do I appeal an Aberdeen property assessment?

Appeals follow the state calendar, and Brown County published its 2026 dates. Assessment notices were due to be mailed by March 1, 2026, and a township informational meeting was set for March 10.

Step2026 date
Notice of appeal to the local board of equalizationMarch 12
Local boards meetMarch 16 to 23
Notice of appeal to the county boardApril 7
County board in sessionApril 14 to May 5
Written notice to Office of Hearing ExaminersMay 15

A circuit court appeal from the county board or the hearing examiners must be filed within 30 days. State law also says that if a board is considering adding omitted property or raising an assessment, it must notify the owner of the time and place so the owner can appear or send written proof.

What city rules could affect an Aberdeen seller?

Aberdeen's Nuisance Vacant Building rules are the main thing to check if a house is empty. In April 2023 the city council took up an ordinance declaring certain vacant buildings a public nuisance and creating a registration program, with responsibilities, enforcement and penalties for owners. Aberdeen's published fee schedule lists a $1,000 annual fee for a new nuisance vacant building registration.

The city also lists Building Inspection, Code Enforcement and a Residential Contractor Board among its departments. Before you sell an empty inherited house, call the city to ask whether it has been flagged, and ask what repairs would be needed to remove a flag.

  • Empty houses can draw code enforcement attention.
  • An inherited or tenant-occupied house can be sold as-is to a cash buyer.
  • A title company will confirm whether any city charges attach to the property before closing.

We buy Aberdeen houses as-is, with no commission, repairs or closing costs to you, and we reply with a written offer you can compare against listing the house.

More questions about Aberdeen, SD

How many people live in Aberdeen, SD?

The Census Bureau estimated 27,961 residents on July 1, 2025, down 1.8% from the April 2020 estimate base of 28,479.

What is the median home value in Aberdeen?

The Census Bureau puts the median value of owner-occupied homes at $217,300 for 2020-2024, with 61.7% of homes owner-occupied.

Which office do I call about Aberdeen property taxes?

Call the Brown County Treasurer at (605) 626-7133, at 25 Market St., Suite 2. For a value question, contact the Brown County Director of Equalization.

What is the South Dakota transfer fee when I sell?

It is $0.50 per $500 of value, or $1.00 per $1,000, under SDCL 43-4-21, and it applies to a deed when there is consideration.

Can I sell a vacant Aberdeen house as-is?

Yes. Check with the city about the Nuisance Vacant Building registration first, then you can sell as-is to a cash buyer without repairs or showings.

Where is Brookings and what is it known for?

Brookings is the county seat of Brookings County, about 60 miles north of Sioux Falls along Interstate 29, and it is best known as the home of South Dakota State University. The city covers roughly 14 square miles at an elevation of 1,660 feet.

The railroad's first train reached Main Street on October 18, 1879, and the city was incorporated on March 9, 1883. It was named for pioneer promoter Wilmot Brookings. The 2020 census counted 23,377 residents, which made it the fourth most populous city in the state.

  • County seat of Brookings County
  • Interstate 29 Exit 132 is the only exit signed for Brookings
  • U.S. Highway 14 also runs through the area

How much does the university shape the Brookings housing market?

South Dakota State University is the state's largest institution of higher education, with 12,065 students enrolled in fall 2024. The school is also the city's largest employer, which gives Brookings a rhythm tied to the academic calendar.

That rhythm shows up in the housing stock. Duplexes, older single-family homes near campus and student rentals sit alongside family neighborhoods on the edge of town. Owners who inherited a rental or who rented to students for years often find themselves selling a house with worn finishes and a tenant lease that runs to a fixed date. Timing a sale around the spring and summer lease cycle can matter more here than in a city without a large campus.

A tight local job market tends to keep demand for homes steady, though it does not guarantee a quick or high-priced sale for a house that needs work.

What does a Brookings winter do to a house?

Brookings has a humid continental climate with long, cold winters, and the numbers explain why heating costs and frozen pipes come up so often. Mean daily temperature runs from 12.8 degrees in January to 70.7 degrees in July.

  • About 35 days a year with lows below zero
  • About 8 days a year at 90 degrees or higher
  • Snowfall of about 35.8 inches a year
  • Precipitation of about 25.21 inches a year, mostly in the warmer months

Cold snaps put stress on furnaces, water heaters and older plumbing. Spring melt tests sump pumps and basement walls. Buyers' inspectors in Brookings routinely look at the furnace age, window condition and signs of water in the lower level. A seller who knows the answers before the inspection is better placed to negotiate.

Is flood risk a factor for Brookings sellers?

It can be for houses near creeks. The city's Engineering Division maintains pages on floodplains and on Six-Mile Creek flood risk mitigation, and the city's future land use map overlays the Six Mile Creek and Deer Creek floodplains.

FEMA publishes the floodplain delineation, so the first step for an owner is to look up the parcel on FEMA's map or ask the city's engineering staff. A buyer will likely ask whether the house is inside it. The seller's disclosure form also asks about flood plains, so the answer has to be written down either way.

What are the rules for rental houses in Brookings?

Brookings inspects and licenses rental dwellings through its Code Enforcement office. Rental properties are inspected and licensed for up to four years, or as an ordinance requires, and each unit is licensed for a maximum number of occupants.

  • The licensing form is the Rental Housing Permit Application.
  • Tenants with occupancy concerns can use the city's complaint form.
  • The city page does not list fees; Code Enforcement can be reached at (605) 692-6629.

A landlord selling a licensed rental should find out when the license expires and what occupant limit applies, because a buyer who plans to keep the tenants will ask. A lapsed license or an old inspection finding is easier to fix before the sale than after a contract is signed.

How and when are Brookings County property taxes paid?

Brookings County collects the first half of the year's property tax by April 30 and the second half by October 31. Taxes can be paid in full once notices go out in January. All special assessments, and any tax bill under $50, are due in full by April 30.

  • Pay in person at 520 3rd Street, Suite 100, Brookings, SD 57006, by mail, online or through the drop box on the west side of the building.
  • Credit cards carry a 2.5 percent service fee at the counter.
  • Mailed payments must be postmarked on or before the due date.
  • Partial payments are not accepted for taxes that are due or delinquent.

The county's Auditor and Treasurer functions share one office. Relief programs listed there include the Disabled Veteran and Surviving Spouse exemption and the Senior Citizens and Disabled assessment freeze. On a sale, the unpaid share of the current bill is normally settled through the title company at closing.

What paperwork does a Brookings sale need?

South Dakota law requires a property condition disclosure from the seller, and the deed needs a Certificate of Real Estate Value (PT 56) before the register of deeds will record it. The state form, dated 07/2025, asks about liens, easements, drainage, the roof, radon, lead paint, mold and the working status of about 47 systems and appliances.

The transfer fee comes from SDCL 43-4-21, and SDCL 43-4-22 lists 19 exemptions. Minnehaha County's schedule shows $1.00 per thousand, and the Brookings County Register of Deeds can confirm its own recording fee and the amount due on your sale.

Which schools and travel options serve Brookings?

Brookings School District 05-1 covers almost all of the city and serves pre-K through grade 12. It enrolled 3,446 students in 2022-23, and its schools include Brookings High School, George S. Mickelson Middle School and Camelot Intermediate. A small part of the city lies in Sioux Valley School District 05-5.

Brookings Regional Airport had a major reconstruction in 2012, and Jefferson Lines offers intercity bus service. Sioux Falls is about 60 miles south on Interstate 29.

When does a cash sale make sense in Brookings?

A cash sale suits a Brookings owner who needs speed or does not want to repair and show a house. Inherited homes, worn student rentals and houses with deferred maintenance are the usual cases.
